newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul to consider $65 mln arena interim finance.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul to consider $65 mln arena interim finance.

text.p: St. Paul Mayor Norm Coleman will ask the City Council to approve a plan to guarantee $65 million interim financing for a new downtown arena if the National Hockey League awards an expansion team, mayoral aides said Wednesday.
St. Paul has already committed to provide $30 million of bonds for a $130 million arena and investors in the group bidding for an expansion team have pledged $35 million.
Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson, a supporter of the arena proposal, has also promised that the state would provide the remaining $65 million of bonds for the project in its bonding bill next year.

The plan introduced to the City Council on Wednesday would give the NHL a solid guarantee of arena financing even if that state money does not materialize, said Erich Mische, Coleman's director of strategic planning.
The City Council will be asked to approve the plan either Friday or Monday, in advance of an NHL expansion committee meeting scheduled for June 4, Mische said.

St. Paul officials have identified four revenue streams to support the debt service on $65 million of general obligation bonds to finance the project "if the worst, but very unlikely, case occurred and the state provided no funding," briefing materials distributed to City Council members stated.

Those sources include revenues from the marquee, an existing 0.5 percent sales tax, hotel/motel tax and existing tax increment financing district, city technology and management services director Martha Larson said.
Revenues from the marquee would support $5.3 million of bonds, the sales tax another $44.5 million, lodging $14 million and TIF district $1.2 million, according to city projections.
St. Paul projections also assume repayment of the ticket and marquee backed bonds over 25 years, the sales and lodging tax backed bonds over 30 years and the TIF district bonds over 10 years.
Minnesota lawmakers failed to reach an accord on $65 million of mostly bond-financed state funding for an arena before closing their session earlier in May.
The NHL has chosen investor groups in St. Paul, Atlanta, Columbus, Ohio, Houston, Nashville and Oklahoma City as finalists for future expansion.
The league has not announced a schedule for expansion or stated how many franchises it will award.
